    # Extract the nonzero rectangular canvas, then recolor the three corner markers
    # according to the external marker arrangement, represented in the object.
    rows=[r for r,row in enumerate(grid) if any(row)]
    cols=[c for c in range(len(grid[0])) if any(grid[r][c] for r in range(len(grid)))]
    r0,r1=min(rows),max(rows); c0,c1=min(cols),max(cols)
    out=[row[c0:c1+1] for row in grid[r0:r1+1]]
    # The outside L of markers maps to object's top-left, top-right, bottom-right.
    # Determine exterior marker colors by their relative positions outside the filled object.
    # Their spatial order is left/top, right/top, right/bottom.
    # Markers in the object are placed at those same three corners.
    # Find exterior singleton colors and use their arrangement (top-left/top-right/bottom-right).
    ext=[]
    for r,row in enumerate(grid):
      for c,v in enumerate(row):
       if v and not (r0<=r<=r1 and c0<=c<=c1): ext.append((r,c,v))
    if len(ext)>=3:
      # map by the three observed exterior points in their spatial order: upper-left, upper-right, lower-right
      ul=min(ext,key=lambda p:p[0]+p[1]); lr=max(ext,key=lambda p:p[0]+p[1])
      ur=max(ext,key=lambda p:p[1]-p[0])
      # In the demos/test these form an L. Use position relative to the exterior bounding box.
      er0=min(p[0] for p in ext); er1=max(p[0] for p in ext); ec0=min(p[1] for p in ext); ec1=max(p[1] for p in ext)
      colors={}
      for r,c,v in ext:
       # align the horizontal/vertical L's endpoints to corresponding object corners
       if r==er0 and c==ec0: colors['tl']=v
       elif r==er0 and c==ec1: colors['tr']=v
       elif r==er1 and c==ec1: colors['br']=v
      # fallback based on points in usual orientation
      if len(colors)<3:
       for r,c,v in ext:
        if (r,c)==(er0,ec0): colors['tl']=v
        elif c==ec1: colors['tr' if r==er0 else 'br']=v
      targets=[(0,0,'tl'),(0,len(out[0])-1,'tr'),(len(out)-1,len(out[0])-1,'br')]
      for rr,cc,k in targets:
       if k in colors and out[rr][cc] in (2,3,4,8): out[rr][cc]=colors[k]
    return out
"

def transform(grid):
    # Trim zero padding to the rectangular canvas.
    rs=[r for r,row in enumerate(grid) if any(row)]
    cs=[c for c in range(len(grid[0])) if any(grid[r][c] for r in range(len(grid)))]
    r0,r1=min(rs),max(rs); c0,c1=min(cs),max(cs)
    obj=[row[c0:c1+1] for row in grid[r0:r1+1]]
    # outside indicators carry replacements for the canvas' three corner markers;
    # identify the outside L endpoints by orientation and map to corner marker positions.
    ext=[(r,c,v) for r,row in enumerate(grid) for c,v in enumerate(row) if v and not(r0<=r<=r1 and c0<=c<=c1)]
    # external colored points: L's two arms share a corner; transfer to the three marked cells
    if len(ext)==3:
        # demo: points (14,8)=3,(14,14)=4,(21,14)=2 ; object corner cells hold 2,4,3
        # external topological endpoints correspond: elbow -> top-left; horizontal endpoint -> top-right; vertical endpoint -> bottom-right
        elbow=max(ext,key=lambda p:sum(1 for q in ext if q!=p and (q[0]==p[0] or q[1]==p[1])))
        arms=[p for p in ext if p!=elbow]
        horizontal=next((p for p in arms if p[0]==elbow[0]),None)
        vertical=next((p for p in arms if p[1]==elbow[1]),None)
        targets=[(0,0,elbow[2]),(0,len(obj[0])-1,horizontal[2] if horizontal else None),(len(obj)-1,len(obj[0])-1,vertical[2] if vertical else None)]
        for r,c,v in targets:
            if v is not None: obj[r][c]=v
    return obj
